history.empty: This repository has no commits yet.
diff.binary: Binary file. There's no text diff to show.
diff.pickFile: Pick a changed file to see its diff.
diff.readOnly: Past commits are read-only. Edit files in Changes.
welcome.title: Welcome to GitLore
welcome.intro: A local workspace for understanding how a codebase changed and why. The demo project TaskFlow is open so you can try everything right away.
welcome.step1: Pick a commit on the left to see exactly what changed.
welcome.step2: Select code in a diff, right-click, and choose Ask GitLore About Selection.
welcome.step3: Ask anything about the history in the assistant on the right.
changes.none: No changes yet. Open a file and edit it to start.
changes.busy: A {op} is in progress in this repository. Finish it in Git first.
assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.slowNote: The first words can take 10–20 seconds on a CPU.
assistant.empty: Ask how and why this code changed. Answers cite the commits they come from; click a citation to open it.
assistant.suggest1: Why did the login switch to JWT tokens?
assistant.suggest2: Which bugs were fixed, and how?
assistant.suggest3: Why was the CSV export reverted?
assistant.noModel: The assistant needs its model: a one-time 1.1 GB download that then runs offline on your CPU.
menu.explainQuestion: Explain this code: what does it do, and why was it changed?
settings.title: Settings
settings.languageNote: Changes the interface and the language the assistant answers in.
settings.modelMissing: Not downloaded yet ({size} GB, one time).
settings.customNote: Any GGUF chat model llama.cpp supports. Larger models answer better but slower.
settings.removeProjectNote: Removing a project only forgets it here. The folder on disk is never touched.
settings.commitCountNote: Newest first. Indexing runs at roughly 25–30 commits per second.
settings.private: Runs locally on your CPU. Nothing leaves this computer.
confirm.removeModel.title: Remove Model?
confirm.removeModel.body: This deletes {file} ({size} GB). You can download it again later.
confirm.removeProject.title: Remove Project?
confirm.removeProject.body: GitLore forgets “{name}” and its chats. The folder on disk is not touched.
confirm.deleteChat.title: Delete Chat?
confirm.deleteChat.body: This deletes “{title}” and all its messages.
confirm.rebuild.title: Rebuild Index?
confirm.rebuild.body: This deletes the index of {n} commits and indexes the repository again.
confirm.discard.title: Discard Unsaved Changes?
confirm.discard.body: {path} has edits that aren't saved yet.
common.offline: GitLore isn't running anymore. Start it again with start.bat (Windows) or start.sh (macOS / Linux).
search.syntax:
Combine words with filters:
author:ada  path:auth  type:security
since:2025-06  until:2025-12  release:v2.0.0  is:large
explain.commitHint: Ask the assistant what this commit changed and why
explain.commitQuestion: Explain this commit: what did it change, and why was it made?
explain.changeQuestion: Explain this change: what does it do, and why was it made?
blame.title: Who Wrote This Code?
blame.note: Share of the {n} current lines, by the person who last changed them.
insights.heatmapSummary: {n} commits in the last year of activity
insights.activitySummary: Hover a month to see what kind of work it was.
insights.categoriesNote: Suggested from commit messages and the files changed. Click one to see its commits.
insights.contributorsNote: Everyone who committed, with the areas they worked on most.
insights.hotNote: Files changed most often. Frequently changed code is where bugs and knowledge concentrate.
insights.noReleases: This repository has no tags yet.
insights.releasesNote: Every tag, newest first, with what changed since the one before.
insights.branchesNote: Local branches, and a comparison of any two branches, tags or commits.
insights.head: To
insights.aheadBehind: {head} has {ahead} commits that {base} doesn't ({behind} the other way).
story.away: What Changed While I Was Away?
story.note: Written by the local AI from commit messages. Every claim cites its commits; a small model can mix things up, so check the cited commits.
story.historyNote: How the project evolved, release by release, and why.
story.stale: Written before the latest changes. Regenerate to include them.
story.notYet: Not written yet. The facts below are ready now.
story.needsModel: Download the model in Settings to have the AI write this.
story.timelineNote: Key moments: releases, security fixes, large changes, reverts, new features and people.
story.awayNote: A short briefing on everything since a date, most important first.
story.onboardingNote: The project in a page, for someone joining or coming back.
online.addNote: Public repositories only, no sign-in. GitLore keeps a read-only copy that updates while it's open.
online.depthNote: Large projects like vscode have 100,000+ commits; start small, you can re-add with more later.
online.noDiscussions: No pull requests or issues are linked to this commit.
settings.onlineNote: Add public GitHub repositories by URL. They stay in sync while GitLore is open; everything else keeps working offline.
settings.onlineToken: GitHub allows 60 anonymous requests per hour. To raise it, set a GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable before starting GitLore; it is never saved.
welcome.introOwn: You're looking at {name}. Browse its history, or let the AI tell its story.
welcome.sinceVisit: {n} new commits since your last visit {when}.
welcome.step4: Open Insights and Story for the big picture: who, what, when and why.
welcome.shortcuts: Ctrl+B hides the sidebar, Ctrl+Alt+B the assistant, Ctrl+K Z enters Zen mode.
